layers.title: Adjustment layers
layers.what: Each layer is one grading tool, and you can stack as many as you like. Lower layers are applied first, upper layers last — just like Photoshop adjustment layers.
layers.tip: Drag layers to reorder. Click the eye to hide one for a quick comparison. Right-click to duplicate or delete.

histogram.title: Histogram
histogram.what: Shows how many pixels sit at each brightness, from darkest (left) to brightest (right). The line is overall luminance; the colored areas are the red, green and blue channels.
histogram.tip: A hill piled on the left means a dark photo, on the right a bright one. A hill cut off at either edge means crushed blacks or blown highlights.

opacity.title: Opacity
opacity.what: How strongly this layer is applied — a discount on the whole effect.
opacity.down: The effect fades, getting closer to how the photo looked without this layer.
opacity.tip: Grading is easy to overdo. Pulling opacity down to 60–80% often looks more natural.

export.quality.title: Quality
export.quality.what: How much JPEG / WebP files are compressed.
export.quality.down: Smaller files, but smooth areas like skies may show blocky banding.
export.quality.tip: 85–92 is plenty for everyday sharing; you can hardly see the difference.

basic.temperature.title: Temperature
basic.temperature.what: Makes the whole photo cooler (blue) or warmer (yellow).
basic.temperature.up: Warmer and more golden, like late-afternoon sun. Feels cozy and nostalgic.
basic.temperature.down: Cooler and bluer, like an overcast morning. Feels calm, quiet and distant.
basic.temperature.tip: First make something that should be white or gray look neutral, then nudge toward the mood you want.

basic.tint.title: Tint
basic.tint.what: Pushes the photo toward green or magenta. Mostly used to fix color casts from artificial light.
basic.tint.up: More magenta and pink. Skin looks rosier; the mood gets dreamy and sweet.
basic.tint.down: More green, like under fluorescent tubes. Fresh in small doses, sickly in large ones.
basic.tint.tip: Indoor shots under office lighting often lean green — a small push to the right fixes it.

basic.exposure.title: Exposure
basic.exposure.what: Overall brightness, measured in stops like a camera. +1 means twice as bright.
basic.exposure.up: Everything gets brighter. Too much turns skies and white walls into blank white.
basic.exposure.down: Everything gets darker — heavier and moodier. Too much turns shadows into mud.
basic.exposure.tip: Set overall brightness with Exposure first, then refine with Highlights and Shadows.

basic.contrast.title: Contrast
basic.contrast.what: How far apart the brights and darks are.
basic.contrast.up: Brights get brighter and darks darker. The image feels punchier and colors get richer.
basic.contrast.down: Tones move closer together. The image softens and turns gray — a gentle, airy look.

basic.highlights.title: Highlights
basic.highlights.what: Adjusts only the bright parts — skies, clouds, lit surfaces.
basic.highlights.up: Bright areas get brighter and the photo feels more open, but sky detail can get lost.
basic.highlights.down: Pulls bright areas down and brings back detail in skies and clouds. The photo feels calmer.
basic.highlights.tip: For any photo with sky, pulling Highlights left almost always helps.

basic.shadows.title: Shadows
basic.shadows.what: Adjusts only the dark parts — backlit faces, shade under trees, corners.
basic.shadows.up: Dark areas open up and reveal detail. The photo feels flatter and more relaxed.
basic.shadows.down: Dark areas get deeper, adding weight and drama.
basic.shadows.tip: For backlit portraits, push Shadows right and the face lights up.

basic.whites.title: Whites
basic.whites.what: Sets how bright the very brightest point is. Works closer to pure white than Highlights.
basic.whites.up: Brighter and cleaner. Too much blows out large areas.
basic.whites.down: The brightest areas turn gray, as if behind a veil — a muted, vintage feel.

basic.blacks.title: Blacks
basic.blacks.what: Sets how dark the very darkest point is.
basic.blacks.up: Black lifts to dark gray — a faded film look.
basic.blacks.down: Deeper blacks. The image feels solid and strong; too much crushes the shadows.

basic.texture.title: Texture
basic.texture.what: Emphasizes or smooths fine detail like pores, leaves, fabric and stone.
basic.texture.up: Crisper, grittier detail — great for landscapes, architecture and character portraits.
basic.texture.down: Fine lines smooth out and skin looks softer, without the plastic look of heavy retouching.
basic.texture.tip: For portraits, −10 to −30 is a natural light skin smoothing.

basic.clarity.title: Clarity
basic.clarity.what: Boosts contrast along the edges of mid-sized shapes, making the image feel more three-dimensional.
basic.clarity.up: Stronger and more rugged. Too much creates halos and a dirty look.

basic.dehaze.title: Dehaze
basic.dehaze.up: Haze disappears, distant things get clearer, colors get richer.
basic.dehaze.down: The scene fills with fog — soft, hazy and atmospheric.
basic.dehaze.tip: On smoggy days, +20 to +40 helps a lot.

basic.vibrance.title: Vibrance
basic.vibrance.what: A “smart” saturation: it boosts only the muted colors and protects skin tones.
basic.vibrance.up: More lively colors, without turning faces orange.
basic.vibrance.down: Colors fade toward a refined, low-saturation look.
basic.vibrance.tip: When you want more color, reach for Vibrance before Saturation.

basic.saturation.title: Saturation
basic.saturation.what: Makes every color stronger or weaker at once.
basic.saturation.up: Richer, louder colors. Too much looks cheap and fake.
basic.saturation.down: Paler colors. All the way left is black and white. Low saturation feels calm and literary.

basic.sharpen.title: Sharpening
basic.sharpen.what: Makes edges crisper so the photo looks sharper.
basic.sharpen.up: Sharper. Too much adds white halos and grain.
basic.sharpen.tip: A little (20–40) before export is enough. Check at 100%.

basic.noise.title: Noise reduction
basic.noise.what: Removes the color speckles and grain in night shots and high-ISO photos.
basic.noise.up: Cleaner and smoother. Too much looks waxy and detail disappears.
basic.noise.down: Keeps the original grain and detail.

basic.vignette.title: Vignette
basic.vignette.what: Darkens or brightens the corners of the photo.
basic.vignette.up: Darker corners pull the eye to the center — focused, cinematic, nostalgic.

basic.grain.title: Grain
basic.grain.up: More visible grain — a film feel with gritty realism.
basic.grain.tip: Grain hides slight softness and noise. Vintage looks often use 20–40.

basic.grainSize.title: Grain size
basic.grainSize.up: Coarser grain, like high-speed film — rough and retro.
basic.grainSize.down: Finer grain that just adds a hint of texture.

layer.curves.title: Curves
layer.curves.what: The most flexible tone and color tool. The horizontal axis is the original brightness, the vertical axis the new one. Lift part of the line to brighten that range, lower it to darken.
layer.curves.tip: Classic moves: an S-curve adds contrast; lifting the bottom-left point gives a faded-film black.

layer.levels.title: Levels
layer.levels.what: Fix tones quickly with three handles — black point, midtone and white point. Simpler than Curves.
layer.levels.tip: If a photo looks gray, press Auto or drag the black and white handles to the ends of the histogram.

layer.hueSaturation.title: Hue/Saturation
layer.hueSaturation.what: Rotates every color, adjusts strength and lightness. Turn on Colorize to tint the whole image a single color.

layer.hsl.title: HSL mixer
layer.hsl.what: Adjusts eight colors separately — turn greens toward teal, deepen only the blue sky, brighten only skin. One of the most-used grading tools.

layer.colorBalance.title: Color balance
layer.colorBalance.what: Adds color separately to shadows, midtones and highlights. Teal shadows plus orange highlights is the classic movie look.

layer.selectiveColor.title: Selective color
layer.selectiveColor.what: The printing-press approach: add or remove cyan, magenta, yellow and black ink in one family of colors (reds, whites, blacks…). Great for fine-tuning a single color.

layer.channelMixer.title: Channel mixer
layer.channelMixer.what: Builds new red, green and blue channels from a recipe of the original ones. Use it for infrared and color-swap effects, or high-quality black and white.

layer.blackWhite.title: Black & white
layer.blackWhite.what: Converts to black and white while letting you decide how bright each color becomes. Darken the blues and the sky turns dramatic.

layer.photoFilter.title: Photo filter
layer.photoFilter.what: Like putting a colored filter in front of the lens — washes the whole photo with a tone.

layer.gradientMap.title: Gradient map
layer.gradientMap.what: Recolors the photo by brightness: the darkest areas take the left color, the brightest take the right. Great for duotone posters and vintage tones.
layer.gradientMap.tip: Drop opacity to 20–40% for a subtle, unified tone.

layer.colorGrading.title: Color grading
layer.colorGrading.what: Three color wheels tint the shadows, midtones and highlights separately — the core tool of film color grading.

layer.posterize.title: Posterize
layer.posterize.what: Reduces the number of tones so the image breaks into flat blocks of color, like a poster or pop art.

layer.threshold.title: Threshold
layer.threshold.what: Turns the photo into pure black and pure white, like a woodcut or silhouette.

layer.invert.title: Invert
layer.invert.what: Black becomes white and every color becomes its complement, like a film negative.

layer.lut.title: Color lookup (LUT)
layer.lut.what: Load a ready-made grade (.cube file) and apply that look in one step. It can sit on top of other adjustments.

layer.brightnessContrast.title: Brightness/Contrast
layer.brightnessContrast.what: The simplest tone adjustment: two sliders for overall brightness and contrast.

layer.exposure.title: Exposure
layer.exposure.what: Adjusts exposure in stops like a camera, with Offset and Gamma as helpers.

layer.vibrance.title: Vibrance
layer.vibrance.what: Adds color intelligently: only to muted colors, while protecting skin.

layer.shadowsHighlights.title: Shadows/Highlights
layer.shadowsHighlights.what: Lifts dark areas and tames bright ones separately, while keeping local contrast. A lifesaver for backlit photos.

layer.hdrToning.title: HDR toning
layer.hdrToning.what: Strengthens local tone and detail for a bold, high-dynamic-range look.

layer.desaturate.title: Desaturate
layer.desaturate.what: Turns the photo grayscale in one step.

layer.matchColor.title: Match color
layer.matchColor.what: Pick a reference photo and this photo's overall color and tone shift toward it. Handy for making a set of photos consistent.

layer.replaceColor.title: Replace color
layer.replaceColor.what: Sample one color from the photo and change only that color's hue, saturation and lightness.

layer.equalize.title: Equalize
layer.equalize.what: Redistributes brightness automatically so dull photos gain separation.

curves.editor.title: Using curves
curves.editor.what: Click the line to add a point, then drag it. The left side controls shadows, the middle midtones, the right highlights.
curves.editor.up: Drag a point up: that brightness range gets brighter (in a red/green/blue channel, it adds that color).
curves.editor.down: Drag a point down: that range gets darker (in a single channel, it adds the opposite color — down in red means more cyan).
curves.editor.tip: Drag a point out of the box to delete it. Fewer points make smoother, more natural curves.

levels.inBlack.title: Input black
levels.inBlack.what: Everything darker than this becomes pure black.
levels.inBlack.up: Deeper shadows and more contrast — gray photos clear up.

levels.gamma.title: Midtones (gamma)
levels.gamma.what: Changes only the middle brightness; pure black and white stay put.
levels.gamma.up: Brighter midtones — lighter, with more shadow detail.

levels.inWhite.title: Input white
levels.inWhite.what: Everything brighter than this becomes pure white.
levels.inWhite.down: Brighter, cleaner highlights — but watch for blowouts.

levels.outBlack.title: Output black
levels.outBlack.what: How dark the darkest point is allowed to be.
levels.outBlack.up: Black turns gray — a faded, vintage look.

levels.outWhite.title: Output white
levels.outWhite.what: How bright the brightest point is allowed to be.
levels.outWhite.down: White turns gray — soft and dim like an old print.

levels.auto.title: Auto
levels.auto.what: Uses the histogram to pull the darkest and brightest points to the ends — one click to clear up a gray photo.

levels.handles.title: Levels handles
levels.handles.what: Under the histogram are three triangles: black is the black point, gray the midtones, white the white point. Drag them directly.
levels.handles.tip: Drag the black and white triangles to where the histogram's hill starts and ends, and the photo clears up.

hs.hue.title: Hue
hs.hue.what: Rotates every color around the color wheel together.
hs.hue.up: Colors shift one way: red → yellow → green…
hs.hue.down: The other way: red → magenta → blue…
hs.hue.tip: Big moves look surreal; small moves fine-tune the overall cast.

hs.saturation.title: Saturation
hs.saturation.down: Paler; all the way left is black and white.

hs.lightness.title: Lightness
hs.lightness.what: Mixes the image toward white or black. Unlike exposure, colors fade as well.
hs.lightness.up: Like a white veil — lighter, paler, lower contrast.
hs.lightness.down: Like a black veil — darker, heavier colors.

hs.colorize.title: Colorize
hs.colorize.what: Turns the whole photo into a single-color tone, like sepia prints or a cold blue.

hs.colorizeHue.title: Colorize hue
hs.colorizeHue.what: Which color the single tone uses.
hs.colorizeHue.tip: Around 30 is nostalgic sepia; 200–220 is a cold blue.

hs.colorizeSat.title: Colorize saturation
hs.colorizeSat.what: How strong the single tone is.
hs.colorizeSat.down: Paler, close to black and white with a hint of tone.

hsl.hue.title: Hue (per color)
hsl.hue.what: Shifts only one color — for example, greens toward yellow or toward teal.
hsl.hue.up: Toward the next color on the wheel (red → orange, green → aqua, blue → purple).
hsl.hue.down: Toward the previous color (orange → red, green → yellow, blue → aqua).
hsl.hue.tip: A common Japanese-style move: greens right toward aqua, then lower their saturation.

hsl.saturation.title: Saturation (per color)
hsl.saturation.up: That color becomes more vivid and eye-catching.
hsl.saturation.down: That color fades and stops stealing attention.
hsl.saturation.tip: If skin looks too red, lower Red and Orange saturation a little.

hsl.luminance.title: Luminance (per color)
hsl.luminance.up: That color gets lighter — skin looks fairer, for example.
hsl.luminance.down: That color gets deeper — a blue sky becomes richer.

cb.tone.title: Tone range
cb.tone.what: Choose whether you're coloring the shadows, midtones or highlights.

cb.magentaGreen.title: Magenta ↔ Green
cb.magentaGreen.up: Greener — fresh and natural; too much looks sickly.

cb.preserve.title: Preserve luminosity
cb.preserve.what: When on, only color changes — adding color won't make the image brighter or darker.

sc.group.title: Color family
sc.group.what: Choose which family of colors to change. Whites, Neutrals and Blacks cover the highlights, mid-grays and shadows.

sc.cyan.title: Cyan
sc.cyan.what: Adds or removes cyan ink in the chosen color.

sc.magenta.title: Magenta
sc.magenta.what: Adds or removes magenta ink in the chosen color.

sc.yellow.title: Yellow
sc.yellow.what: Adds or removes yellow ink in the chosen color.

sc.black.title: Black
sc.black.what: Adds or removes black ink in the chosen color.
sc.black.up: That color gets deeper, darker, more solid.
sc.black.down: That color gets lighter, brighter, more transparent.

sc.mode.title: Relative / Absolute
sc.mode.what: Relative scales the ink already there, so changes are gentler. Absolute adds or removes a fixed amount, so changes are stronger.

cm.output.title: Output channel
cm.output.what: Choose which channel you're rebuilding: red, green or blue.

cm.red.title: Red source
cm.red.what: How much of the original red channel goes into this output channel.
cm.red.up: Areas that were red get brighter in this channel.
cm.red.down: Areas that were red get darker in this channel.

cm.green.title: Green source
cm.green.what: How much of the original green channel goes into this output channel.
cm.green.up: Areas that were green get brighter in this channel.
cm.green.down: Areas that were green get darker in this channel.

cm.blue.title: Blue source
cm.blue.what: How much of the original blue channel goes into this output channel.
cm.blue.up: Areas that were blue get brighter in this channel.
cm.blue.down: Areas that were blue get darker in this channel.

cm.constant.title: Constant
cm.constant.what: Adds a fixed amount to this channel everywhere.
cm.constant.up: The whole image gets more of this channel's color (red constant up → warmer red cast).
cm.constant.down: The whole image loses this color (red constant down → cyan cast).

cm.mono.title: Monochrome
cm.mono.what: Outputs black and white, using the channel mix to decide how each tone renders.
cm.mono.tip: Keep the three numbers adding up to about 100% to match the original brightness.

bw.tint.title: Tint
bw.tint.what: Washes the black and white with a color, like an old sepia print.

bw.tintHue.title: Tint hue
bw.tintHue.what: Which color to tint with. Around 30 is sepia, around 210 a cold blue.

bw.tintSat.title: Tint saturation
bw.tintSat.down: Closer to pure black and white.

pf.color.title: Filter color
pf.color.what: The color of the filter in front of the lens. Warm colors warm the image; cool colors calm it.

pf.density.title: Density
pf.density.what: How deep the filter color is.
pf.density.up: Stronger tint — the whole image takes on the color.

pf.preserve.title: Preserve luminosity
pf.preserve.what: When on, the filter won't darken the image. When off, it behaves like real glass in front of the lens and darkens slightly.

gm.stops.title: Color stops
gm.stops.what: Each color point on the gradient. The left color goes to the darkest parts of the photo, the right color to the brightest.
gm.stops.tip: Deep blue shadows with warm yellow highlights is the classic movie-poster duotone.

gm.position.title: Position
gm.position.what: Which brightness this color is placed at.

gm.reverse.title: Reverse
gm.reverse.what: Flips the gradient, swapping the shadow and highlight colors.

cg.wheel.title: Color wheel
cg.wheel.what: Drag the dot: its direction chooses the color, its distance from the center sets how strong it is. Double-click the wheel to reset.
cg.wheel.tip: A common film look: shadows a little toward teal, highlights a little toward orange.

cg.hue.title: Hue
cg.hue.what: Which color to add to this tone range — the same as the direction on the wheel.

cg.saturation.title: Strength
cg.saturation.what: How strong the added color is.

cg.luminance.title: Luminance
cg.luminance.what: Brightens or darkens this tone range.

cg.blending.title: Blending
cg.blending.what: How wide the transitions between shadows, midtones and highlights are.
cg.blending.up: Softer transitions; the three colors blend together.
cg.blending.down: Sharper boundaries; the three colors stay distinct.

cg.balance.title: Balance
cg.balance.what: Moves the dividing line between shadows and highlights.
cg.balance.up: The highlight color covers more of the image.
cg.balance.down: The shadow color covers more of the image.

poster.levels.title: Levels
poster.levels.what: How many brightness steps each channel keeps.
poster.levels.up: More steps — closer to the original.
poster.levels.down: Fewer, bigger blocks — stronger poster and pop-art feel.

threshold.level.title: Threshold
threshold.level.what: Anything darker than this becomes black, anything brighter becomes white.

lut.intensity.title: Intensity
lut.intensity.what: How strongly the LUT is applied.
lut.intensity.down: A lighter look, blended with the original.
lut.intensity.tip: Downloaded LUTs are often heavy; around 70% usually ages better.

wb.eyedropper.title: White balance picker
wb.eyedropper.what: Click something in the photo that should be white or gray (a white wall, a white shirt, gray pavement). Lumen works out the temperature and tint that make it neutral.
wb.eyedropper.tip: Don't click blown-out pure white — there's no color information left there.

calib.shadowTint.title: Shadow tint
calib.shadowTint.what: Adds a touch of green or magenta to the very darkest tones, to fix shadow casts some cameras produce.
calib.shadowTint.up: Shadows lean magenta — warmer and softer.
calib.shadowTint.down: Shadows lean green — a slightly cool, filmic feel.

calib.hue.title: Primary hue
calib.hue.what: Changes how the camera reads this primary color. It affects every color that contains it, so it's broader and more fundamental than HSL.
calib.hue.up: This primary shifts toward the next color on the wheel (red → orange, green → aqua, blue → purple).
calib.hue.down: The other way (red → magenta, green → yellow, blue → aqua).
calib.hue.tip: A secret of many film looks: blue primary hue left and saturation right — skin tones get clearer.

calib.saturation.title: Primary saturation
calib.saturation.what: Raises or lowers the purity of this primary color overall.
calib.saturation.up: Every color containing it gets richer.
calib.saturation.down: Every color containing it gets paler and quieter.

bc.brightness.title: Brightness
bc.brightness.what: Overall lighter or darker, mostly in the midtones. The brightest and darkest points barely move.

bc.contrast.title: Contrast
bc.contrast.what: The gap between light and dark.

exp.exposure.title: Exposure
exp.exposure.what: Adjusts brightness in stops in linear light, like a camera. The brightest areas change the most.
exp.exposure.up: Brighter overall; highlights blow out more easily.

exp.offset.title: Offset
exp.offset.what: Adds or subtracts a fixed amount from every pixel, mostly affecting shadows.
exp.offset.up: Shadows lift — the image gets gray and hazy.

exp.gamma.title: Gamma correction
exp.gamma.what: Bends the middle of the tone curve; pure black and white stay put.

sh.shadowsAmount.title: Shadow amount
sh.shadowsAmount.what: How much the dark areas are lifted.
sh.shadowsAmount.up: More shadow detail — flatter and more open.

sh.highlightsAmount.title: Highlight amount
sh.highlightsAmount.what: How much the bright areas are pulled down.
sh.highlightsAmount.up: Skies and bright surfaces regain their detail.

sh.radius.title: Radius
sh.radius.what: How large an area is looked at to decide whether something counts as bright or dark.
sh.radius.up: More natural, global transitions, but less local contrast.
sh.radius.down: Finer control, but halos may appear along edges.

sh.colorCorrection.title: Color correction
sh.colorCorrection.what: Lifting or darkening areas can make their color paler or stronger; this compensates.

sh.midtoneContrast.title: Midtone contrast
sh.midtoneContrast.what: Lifting shadows can flatten the image; this brings midtone punch back.

hdr.radius.title: Edge glow radius
hdr.radius.what: How wide the local enhancement reaches.
hdr.radius.up: Large-scale light and dark contrast — dramatic, with halos along edges.

hdr.strength.title: Edge glow strength
hdr.strength.what: How hard local contrast is pushed.
hdr.strength.up: A stronger, more exaggerated HDR feel.

hdr.gamma.title: Gamma
hdr.gamma.what: Overall distribution of light and dark.

hdr.detail.title: Detail
hdr.detail.what: How sharp the fine textures are.
hdr.detail.up: Very crisp, gritty texture with a strong HDR feel.

mc.intensity.title: Color intensity
mc.intensity.down: Paler colors; all the way left is nearly grayscale.

mc.fade.title: Fade
mc.fade.what: Blends the matched result back with the original.
mc.fade.up: Closer and closer to the original.

mc.neutralize.title: Neutralize
mc.neutralize.what: Removes the reference photo's own color cast, borrowing only its tone and color separation.

rc.fuzziness.title: Fuzziness
rc.fuzziness.what: How close a color must be to the target to be replaced.
rc.fuzziness.up: A wider range — similar colors get replaced too.
rc.fuzziness.down: A narrower range — only very close colors.
rc.fuzziness.tip: First swing Hue to an extreme to see exactly what's selected, then tune Fuzziness.

rc.hue.title: Replacement hue
rc.hue.what: Moves the selected color to another spot on the color wheel.

eq.recompute.title: Recalculate
eq.recompute.what: Equalize is measured from the image at the moment the layer was added. If you've changed the adjustments below it since, click here to measure again.

bw.red.title: Reds
bw.red.what: How bright things that were reds become in the black-and-white image.
bw.red.tip: For portraits, push Reds right for clearer, brighter skin.

bw.yellow.title: Yellows
bw.yellow.what: How bright things that were yellows become in the black-and-white image.

bw.green.title: Greens
bw.green.what: How bright things that were greens become in the black-and-white image.

bw.cyan.title: Cyans
bw.cyan.what: How bright things that were cyans become in the black-and-white image.

bw.blue.title: Blues
bw.blue.what: How bright things that were blues become in the black-and-white image.
bw.blue.tip: Pull Blues left and the sky goes dark with standout clouds — the classic dramatic black and white.

bw.magenta.title: Magentas
bw.magenta.what: How bright things that were magentas become in the black-and-white image.
